questions.explain: (N) Listen to a talk in a business class. [2 second pause] (W-Am) Let’s talk about corporate governance. Corporate governance is the way a company is governed and managed. It’s like a set of rules and practices that help make sure the company runs smoothly and fairly. It’s important because it helps balance the needs of groups like shareholders, managers, customers, and suppliers. One key part of corporate governance is the board of directors. This group makes major decisions about where the company is headed. A strong board is often made up of people with diverse backgrounds—for example, individuals with experience in finance, law, operations, or marketing. This mix of expertise helps the board look at issues from different angles and make more informed decisions. Another important part is ensuring transparency. This means the company should be open and honest about what it’s doing and how it’s performing. One major way companies show transparency is through financial reports. Companies should regularly share financial reports to show how they’re doing financially, and also explain any risks they’re facing. When companies are transparent, it builds trust and helps investors feel more confident. Of course, putting good corporate governance into practice isn’t always easy. It takes effort and money—the cost of hiring outside experts to check the company’s finances could be high. And you’ll need to set up systems in advance to make sure rules are being followed. [2 second pause]

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention financial reports?

options.A: To compare financial strategies across industries
options.B: To show how businesses increase their profits
options.C: To outline how companies reduce expenses
options.D: To explain that honest disclosures earn trust
